name: HULO Geo-block
author: huloglobal

sections.description:
HULO Geo-block decides, before WordPress runs its main query, whether a visitor may use your site. Allowed visitors are untouched; refused visitors see a branded block page or are redirected.

Works on any WordPress site. If you take payments with the free HULO Payments plugin, payments from blocked visitors are refused before they are charged.

Rules

  • Region presets: Worldwide, United Kingdom only, European Union, North America and Oceania.
  • Extra allowed countries and always-blocked countries (for example “the EU except one country”, or “worldwide except a few”).
  • A live, plain-English summary of what the rules do, and a warning before you save rules that would block everyone.

Never locks you out

  • Administrators are never blocked.
  • wp-admin, the login page, cron, AJAX, the REST API, XML-RPC, payment-gateway callbacks (wc-api), robots.txt and sitemaps are never blocked.
  • IP allowlist with IPv4 and IPv6 addresses and CIDR ranges, plus a one-click “Add my IP”.

SEO-safe

  • Well-known search and link-preview crawlers (Googlebot, Bingbot, DuckDuckBot, Applebot, Facebook, LinkedIn, Slack, WhatsApp and more) are let through by default, so a country restriction does not drop your site out of search results. Permissive, custom and off modes are available.
  • Crawlers may only browse. A User-Agent can be faked, so add-to-cart, checkout and payments are never exempt.
  • Optional reverse-DNS verification of Googlebot and Bingbot: a visitor claiming to be one is checked against googlebot.com / search.msn.com before it is let through.
  • Block pages send noindex; closures (business hours, maintenance) send HTTP 503 with Retry-After so search engines treat them as temporary.

Business hours and maintenance

  • A weekly opening window in any time zone, including overnight windows and daylight saving.
  • A one-off maintenance window with its own allowed IPs and optional message. The “back soon” page shows when the window ends, and Retry-After tells search engines the same.

Geolocation without external calls

  • Cloudflare CF-IPCountry (and cf-region-code), Akamai and Fastly country headers, once you tell the plugin the site is behind that CDN. Any visitor can send these headers, so they are honoured only for requests arriving from a trusted proxy: Cloudflare’s published ranges (one tick) or the addresses you list (or the HULO_TRUSTED_PROXIES constant).
  • Web-server GeoIP modules (GEOIP_COUNTRY_CODE, MM_COUNTRY_CODE).
  • This plugin never calls a geolocation API. If no source is available yet, the settings page says so and visitors with an unknown country are allowed.
  • A full country list ships with the plugin.
  • Proxy-aware visitor IP: by default only the connecting address is used. Forwarding headers you tick are read only from trusted proxies, and for X-Forwarded-For the right-most address that is not one of your proxies is taken.

Cache-safe

  • Only refused responses are changed, and they are sent with no-store and DONOTCACHEPAGE, so no page cache stores a block page.
  • Optional page-cache helper: if a full-page cache serves pages without running WordPress, a small script re-checks the visitor against an uncached endpoint.

Headless storefronts

  • GET /wp-json/hulo-geo-block/v1/check returns the current visitor’s verdict (uncached). A server-side caller can pass the visitor’s country signed with a secret.
  • The endpoint is rate-limited per visitor IP: 120 requests a minute by default, configurable on the Settings tab (requests and window, or off when a CDN or firewall already limits it). Over the limit it answers 429 with Retry-After.

With WooCommerce

Geo-block also:

  • refuses add-to-cart, the classic checkout and the Checkout block (Store API) for blocked visitors, on the server, whatever a page cache served;
  • never blocks shop managers;
  • can use the shop’s geolocation, including its MaxMind database integration, as a country source;
  • uses the shop’s translated country names.

Geo-block Pro

The optional Pro add-on adds 32 more region presets (EEA, Schengen, EFTA, GCC, ASEAN, LATAM, APAC, Commonwealth and more), rules for 249 states, provinces and regions in 11 countries, a soft block that lets visitors browse with a notice but not buy, an audit log with blocked-traffic stats and a dashboard widget, a rule simulator and a weekly e-mail report. Try it free for 14 days, no card: huloglobal.com/wordpress-plugins/geo-block.

External services

This plugin does not connect to any external service. Country lookups use request headers set by your CDN or web server or, when WooCommerce is active, its own geolocation. Its MaxMind integration, if you turn it on, downloads the GeoLite2 database from MaxMind itself, under MaxMind’s terms; this plugin never does.

If you turn on “Verify Googlebot and Bingbot by reverse DNS” (off by default), a visitor whose User-Agent claims to be Googlebot or Bingbot has their IP address looked up in DNS (a reverse lookup, then a forward lookup of the returned host name) through your server’s own DNS resolver. The answer is cached for a day. Only the visitor’s IP address is involved; no data is sent to Google, Microsoft or HULO.
sections.installation:
1. Install HULO Geo-block from Plugins → Add New, or upload the zip, and activate it.
  2. Go to HULO → Geo-block. If the page says no country source was found, put the site behind a CDN that sends the visitor’s country (for example Cloudflare) and set it up on the Settings tab (country headers and trusted proxies), or enable a GeoIP module in your web server. On a WooCommerce shop you can instead add a MaxMind licence key in its Integration settings.
  3. On the Rules tab pick the regions or countries you serve, tick “Apply the country rules to visitors” and save.
sections.faq:
Can I lock myself out?

No. Administrators are never blocked, wp-admin and the login page are never blocked, and the plugin will not switch on rules that would allow no one.

Do I need WooCommerce?

No. Geo-block works on any WordPress site. If you do run it, Geo-block also guards add-to-cart and checkout and can use the shop’s MaxMind geolocation.

What happens when a visitor’s country is unknown?

They are allowed; allowlists, business hours and maintenance still work. Set up a country source (see Installation, step 2) so countries are known.

Does it work with page caching?

Yes. Block pages are never cached. If your cache serves HTML without running WordPress, turn on the page-cache helper on the Settings tab. Checkout and payments always re-check the visitor on the server.

Will Google still index my site?

Yes, by default search and link-preview crawlers are let through.

Can a visitor fake their country or pretend to be Googlebot?

Country headers are only believed when the request comes from a proxy you trust, so a visitor cannot send their own. A crawler User-Agent only lets a visitor browse, never buy or pay, and with reverse-DNS verification on, a fake Googlebot or Bingbot is treated like any other visitor.

Does the plugin contact any external service?

No. See “External services” below.
sections.changelog:
0.1.3

  • Redesigned block, closed and maintenance pages: a clean centred card with your logo (or the theme’s logo or site icon, or the site name), a coloured bar, your message, the visitor’s location on country blocks, and your support e-mail as a button. Accessible markup: a main landmark, one heading, readable contrast and visible keyboard focus.
  • New optional accent colour on the Block page tab (default blue). Text on the accent switches to black or white automatically so it stays readable.
  • New optional maintenance message. Left blank, the page uses the Block page message as before.
  • Fix: the closed and maintenance pages had the title “Not available in your region” and a “Not available” badge. They now have their own wording.
  • The maintenance page’s Retry-After now matches the end of the window (at least a minute, at most a day) instead of always one hour.
  • The Block page tab previews the country, maintenance and closed pages.
  • “Add my IP” now says so when your address cannot be read.
  • Tested with WooCommerce 11.3.

0.1.2

  • Configurable rate limit for the public check endpoint (requests per visitor IP and window length, 0 to switch it off) on the Settings tab, with a hulo_geo_block_rate_limit filter. The 429 answer’s Retry-After now says when the window resets.

0.1.1

  • Security: crawler User-Agents may browse but never buy or pay; CDN country and IP headers are honoured only from trusted proxies (off by default); REST, wc-api and wc-ajax exemptions follow what WordPress actually routed; optional reverse-DNS verification of Googlebot and Bingbot.
  • The block page’s styles are registered and printed through WordPress, and settings forms read and sanitise each declared field.

0.1.0

  • First release for any WordPress site: country and region-preset rules, always-blocked countries, IP allowlist (IPv4/IPv6 CIDR), crawler allowlist, branded block page or redirect, business hours, maintenance window, CDN/web-server geolocation, bundled country list, page-cache helper, headless check endpoint and extension hooks.
  • With HULO Payments: payments from blocked visitors are refused. With WooCommerce: add-to-cart and checkout guards (classic and Checkout block) and its MaxMind geolocation.
